title: Matched HadSST4 coverage retains positive OISST v2.1 trend gaps in the east Pacific and at 50-60 S in 1982-2022
abstract: We tested whether changing in situ coverage accounts for regional SST trend differences. We remapped four pinned SST records to five-degree cells and separated the monthly sampling effect from the product difference on matched cells and months. In 1982-2022, OISST v2.1 minus HadSST4 on matched samples has trends of +0.0245 C per decade in the east equatorial Pacific and +0.0588 at 50-60 S. Conditional 95 percent intervals are 0.0058 to 0.0422 and 0.0364 to 0.0802. Monthly coverage effects are -0.0012 and +0.0139. The Southern Ocean baseline rule retains 72.1 percent of the ice-free target area. Rules that retain 95.1 or 24.1 percent also give positive matched differences. In situ reconstructions still disagree after matching. Individual east-Pacific trend intervals include zero, and its 2001-2022 paired difference is unresolved. Thus coverage matching supports a relative trend discrepancy but does not establish absolute cooling or identify the erroneous product. Source bias, shared observations, within-cell sampling and reference uncertainty remain. Code, source hashes, fit tables, coverage summaries, a figure and independent numerical checks support reproduction. External grids and derived monthly records are not bundled.

display.caption: The 1982-2022 trend difference from HadSST4 is split into a monthly sampling effect and a difference on matched cells and months. Error bars are conditional pointwise 95 percent intervals. The 50-60 S panel uses 72.1 percent of the fixed ice-free target area.
